steps.text: Set an oven rack 4 to 6 inches from the heat source and preheat the oven's broiler. Grease a broiler pan or line pan with aluminum foil.

Combine Parmesan cheese, mayonnaise, butter, and lemon juice in a small bowl; season with basil, black pepper, onion powder, and celery salt. Mix well; set aside. Arrange fillets in a single layer on the prepared pan.
Broil for 4 to 6 minutes, flipping fillets halfway. Remove fillets from oven; coat top side with Parmesan mixture. Continue broiling until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 2 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Broiled Tilapia Parmesan
raw_recipe.description: This healthier broiled tilapia Parmesan recipe uses light mayonnaise and less butter for a healthier version of tilapia. It makes a quick and easy meal.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a healthier version of broiled Parmesan-crusted tilapia. It calls for less butter and a light mayonnaise. And if you prefer, you can substitute olive oil for the butter.

review.reviewBody: VERRRRY tasty! I had made a few diferent Tilapia recipies with my frozen bag of fillets from Sams, and this is my FAVORITE! :D I had never even broiled something before, if that helps show how easy it was as well. Most definitely making this again. I'll post my picture soon too!

I made this recipe with fresh caught tilapia. I wasn't sure at first, when mixing the ingredients together. I followed the recipe exactly. I served it over white rice with fresh green beans. It turned out absolutely amazing! After taking the fish from the pan there was some juice still left in the pan. I poured it into a small sauce pan and added some heavy whipping cream, lemon juice and a bit of sea salt (small amounts of each). I spooned the sauce over the fish and rice, and the result... 5 star restaurant quality meal!!!!! It was absolutely amazing! I'm glad I found this recipe! Will be making this again, and often! Thanks!!!!

Pretty tastyI I haven't made the regular version of "Broiled Tilapia Parmesan" so I can't compare the two, but this topping held its own during the cooking process. I decided to bake the fish at 375 degrees for 10 minutes without the topping and then another 8-9 after the topping was spread on the fillets. I added Paul Prudhomme's "Seafood Magic" to the seasoning mix and probably upped the amounts of the other seasonings. I always sprinkle lemon pepper on my fillets regardless of the recipe. I used olive oil instead of the butter.

This is a fast, easy recipe that wins every time. I broil it at 400 degrees with a little of the sauce on one side, then turn it, add the rest of the sauce, and cook til done. 4 to 5 minutes each side.

Absolutely my favorite tilapia recipe ever!!! I almost licked my plate afterwards. Have been this at least 10 times already. Tips: I followed the recipe exactly except I don't have celery salt but had celery seeds and salt and just used equal parts of both. Also when you put it back in, I put it back in on broil for 5 minutes, not 3, to get it nice and brown toasted. I also sometimes double the celery seed and onion because I love my for extra seasoned. Just finger-licking good!!! And great for those watching calories. Great protein and low cal. Winner!
Delicious! My husband who doesn't like fish enjoyed it. I did leave out the butter and just brushed the fish with olive oil and added some bread crumbs. Definitely a do over.

Excellent recipe! I only had two large tilapia but didn't change the ingredient amounts and it worked out fine. I didn't have celery salt (excluded the cheese) but did add Greek seasoning and just a sprinkling of bread crumbs. Mine was in the oven at 350 for 20 minutes. It has a light yet flavorful taste.

We love this! Making it regularly now. The key is reapAs other reviewers recommended, I add hot pepper flakes (a quarter tps or so) and about a quarter cup panel bread crumbs. And sprinkle fish with old bay before broiling. This is wonderful!

I go back to this recipe again and again. I sprinkle Old Bay seasoning on the filets before putting on the topping. Instead of broiling you can bake the filets for approx 15 minutes (depending on size of filet). Have also substituted other white fish (swai) for tilapia. Yum.
Excellent, simple recipe! One slight adjustment next time...6 minutes total cook time...to keep it moist.

This turned out so DELICIOUS! My family loved it and ate 2 pans of it for dinner, and there's only 4 of us!
I'm going to try it with bread crumbs mixed in next time for a bit of a crunch. I cooked it til it was dark golden brown and crispy around the edges. I also doubled the recipe for about 3 lbs of tilapia.
I think if i use olive oil instead of butter that I'll try adding honey and cut the oil in half or completely out. Talk about healthy! 
This has worked well with salmon.
Great flavor and a quick meal! My husband and I both loved it. I didn't have celery salt so I just added a pinch of regular salt.

This is absolutely my new favorite fish recipe. Full disclosure, I did not have LF mayo and used regular, so there's that. I also browned mine up more than in the pic. I added lemon pepper as well. Phenomenal flavor!
Great, but add more parm and salt next time.
I really liked this recipe although I found it to be a little salty..I will make it again but add less parmesan cheese and no extra salt..
Quick and easy, we really enjoyed this! No edits, it's perfect as written. - March 2024

The sauce was more fluid than I had expected, but the fish was extraordinary. Even my wife (who is extraordinarily spoiled) was impressed. Served with fresh broccoli broiled in walnut oil and black walnuts.
Delicious!!! Quick easy and a tasty dinner. I make this pretty often even my kids love it. I use even less butter than instructed and sometimes none at all.
I enjoyed this simple recipe and the citrus flavor did come through. I did sprinkle some plain bread crumbs on top.
